assess.title: Assess the mathematical problem
assess.objective: Read the exact problem and references, initialize mathematical memory, extract assumptions, identify terminology, and decide the first balanced retrieval/reasoning actions.
rules: Use the complete original statement as authoritative input.
Do not claim the problem is impossible merely because it may be open.
Record cheap deductions and a concrete initial search/reasoning plan.
Separate verified facts, hypotheses, conjectures, and unknowns.

explore.title: Explore results, examples, counterexamples, and proof directions
explore.objective: Combine deep independent reasoning with mathematical retrieval, toy examples, counterexample testing, and memory reuse before selecting decomposition plans.
rules: Search nontrivial claims, but stop leaning on retrieval when it no longer helps.
When using an external result, record its complete statement and identifiers and check local definitions and assumptions.
Analyze partial results by explaining their extra hypotheses and where their methods fail for the full problem.
Construct toy examples and actively test fragile claims with counterexamples.
Persist every important conclusion, obstruction, and failed path.

propose_plans.title: Propose materially different decomposition plans
propose_plans.objective: Create at least two distinct proof strategies, each with ordered subgoals, motivation, dependencies, and known risks.
rules: Plans must be materially different rather than cosmetic rewrites.
Each plan must state how it avoids known counterexamples and failed paths.
Each plan must be directly screenable subgoal by subgoal.

direct_proving.title: Directly screen every active decomposition plan
direct_proving.objective: Attempt all subgoals of each active plan, reuse relevant examples and references, and identify exact stuck points before requesting isolated branch work.

commit_payload_contract.screening: Submit any completed subset keyed by server-issued plan_id and subgoal_id. Each subgoal result needs solved|partial|stuck status and a non-empty summary. Partial submissions are retained and return exact missing ids without advancing state.
server_derives: all-active-plan branch set when no plan is completely solved
stuck-point summaries from non-solved subgoal reports
solved_fields: selected_plan_id only when multiple plans are completely solved

rules: Try to carry each whole plan through before abandoning it.
When stuck on a subgoal, test the subgoal with counterexamples immediately.
Record solved, partial, and stuck status for every subgoal using the server-issued ids in the task context.
If screening is incomplete, submit the available reports and continue with the missing ids returned by the server instead of reconstructing the entire report.
A completely solved plan must provide a full-proof route; if exactly one plan is solved the server selects it automatically.
A recursive round begins only after every active plan and subgoal has been screened; the server creates one branch for every active plan without requiring branch_plans to be echoed.

branch_run.title: Work independently on one assigned proof plan
branch_run.objective: Use the frozen snapshot and assigned plan only, deepen or locally refine that plan, and return either a complete proof route or precise failure evidence.
rules: Do not request or infer another branch's result before the join barrier.
Preserve continuity with the assigned plan rather than restarting from zero.
Record all progress and failures in branch-local memory.
Return a structured result with status solved, partial, or failed.

branch_join.title: Join the sealed branch results
branch_join.objective: Compare every branch from the same frozen snapshot, select a complete route if one exists, or synthesize common failure information for replanning.

commit_payload_contract.server_derives_outcome: solved when a solved selected branch or synthesis_proof_route exists; otherwise failed
commit_payload_contract.considered_branch_ids: Optional audit hint only; complete sealed-branch coverage is derived by the server.
commit_payload_contract.solved_requires: If exactly one branch is solved the server selects it automatically; multiple solved branches require selected_branch_id or synthesis_proof_route.

rules: Read all sealed results before selecting a route.
Do not merge incompatible claims without rechecking them.
If no branch succeeds, identify recurring obstructions and evidence rather than merely saying the problem is hard.

identify_failures.title: Synthesize the key failures
identify_failures.objective: Turn failed direct and branch attempts into reusable constraints for the next planning generation.
rules: List plan-specific stuck points and common obstructions.
Distinguish false subgoals, missing hypotheses, missing background, and merely incomplete arguments.
State concrete implications for the next plan set.

replan.title: Prepare a new planning generation
replan.objective: Use accumulated failure knowledge, counterexamples, and successful partial steps to define a materially improved search space.
rules: Do not repeat a failed plan unchanged.
Explain what new information justifies each new direction.
Preserve useful partial lemmas even when their original plans failed.

assemble.title: Assemble a complete self-contained LaTeX proof
assemble.objective: Write draft/proof.tex as a single compilable document containing the complete target statement and full proof in dependency order.
rules: The document must be self-contained and must not use input/include or shell escape.
Supporting definitions, lemmas, and propositions precede statements that use them.
The final target theorem appears last and repeats the complete original statement.
External results include complete statements, paper identifiers, theorem identifiers, and arXiv identifiers when available.

verify.title: Verify the complete proof independently
verify.objective: Audit the proof sequentially, check every small inference and external reference, and report every critical error and gap under a strict accept rule.

commit_payload_contract.memory_preconditions: At least one statement_checks record and one audit event. If the proof cites external results, reference_checks must also be non-empty.
commit_payload_contract.verification_report: summary plus complete critical_errors and gaps arrays; wrong findings require repair_hints.

rules: Do not access generation memory, branches, steering, or generator confidence.
Check exact definitions, formulas, quantifiers, assumptions, and object existence.
Check external statements and the transition from each statement to its use.
Persist sequential statement checks and an audit-complete event before submitting the report.
When the proof declares citations or theorem identifiers, persist reference checks before submitting the report.
A proof is correct only when both critical_errors and gaps are empty.
The server, not the verifier model, computes the final verdict.

repair.title: Repair the proof using the verifier report
repair.objective: Resolve every critical error and gap, changing strategy or backtracking when a local edit cannot repair the proof.

commit_payload_contract.proof: The full replacement proof must differ from the last proof that received a wrong verdict.

rules: Resolve critical errors first and then all remaining gaps.
Do not assume every repair is local.
Record invalidated paths and new decisions.
Do not resubmit the exact proof bytes that just failed verification.
Resubmit the entire proof through LaTeX and verification gates.
